scope: All integer representatives of one fixed simultaneous-nonresidue CRT class d0 modulo the complete fixed-M j=1 candidate product B_M
proved: The simultaneous-nonresidue class d0 modulo B is fixed before Archimedean optimization; cross-class optimization is not included.
In the nonempty-candidate case B>1 and y!=0, the representative norms are the affine lattice N_k=t-kq with t=x^2-d0*y^2 and q=B*y^2.
The exact global minimum is dist(t,qZ)=min(r,q-r), where r is the least nonnegative residue of t modulo q; the minimizing representative is obtained by nearest-integer division.
For a nonzero pair with B>1 and y!=0, the minimum is positive and the minimizing k is unique.
Writing c=gcd(abs(x),abs(y)), x=cX, and y=cY gives gcd(X^2-d0*Y^2,B*Y^2)=1.
Every representative norm factors as c^2 times a cofactor coprime to the complete candidate product B.
For every candidate prime p and every representative, v_p(x^2-d*y^2)=2*v_p(c); changing representatives never changes candidate-prime valuation.
The gcd of two adjacent representative norms, and hence the ideal generated by all representatives, is exactly c^2.
Unrestricted Bezout recombination therefore returns Item281's original specialized Fitting/gcd target squared, not a new invariant.
The exact balanced value is mu=c^2*mu_prime with gcd(mu_prime,B*Y^2)=1 and 1<=mu_prime<B*Y^2/2.
The one-dimensional fixed-class covering-radius bound is mu<B*y^2/2; an exponential improvement requires special arithmetic information about the actual residue phase.

For a natural product of e independently chosen same-class representative norms, the minimum absolute product is mu^e and every candidate valuation is multiplied by e, so the divisor-to-height ratio is unchanged.
The adjacent difference B*y^2 is divisible by all candidate primes and therefore loses exact collision recognition.
Using only the frozen component bounds and log B=M/6+o(M), the optimal representative reproduces the normalized ratio H-kappa+1/12 and raw ratio H/2+1/24.
A useful normalized absolute-height theorem would require log mu<(1/3-epsilon)M; no such theorem is proved.
Item149 de-overlap leaves the fixed-j1 ceiling unchanged at 1/36 per 6M.

fixed_class_theorem.input: one frozen d0 modulo B with Legendre(d0,p)=-1 for every p|B
fixed_class_theorem.representatives: d=d0+kB for arbitrary k in Z
fixed_class_theorem.factorization_independent_algorithm: nearest Euclidean quotient; no factorization of the norm and no collision subset query

primitive_decomposition.coprimality: gcd(T,Q)=1 and gcd(T-kQ,Q)=1 for every k
primitive_decomposition.candidate_valuation: 2*v_p(c) for every p|B and every representative

boundary_branches.B_one: candidate set empty and prime-log mass zero; a representative norm may vanish
